images.title: Building a dot plot
images.purpose: Recap how to build a dot plot: equal steps on a line, one dot per value, equal values stacked, and the range read from the ends.
images.composition: One short number line across the lower middle of the frame with a few stacked dots above it and a range bracket below it; the rest is white space.
exact_structure: A dark grey (#2B2B2B) horizontal number line from 2 to 9 with 8 equally spaced ticks, each numbered: 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9.
7 teal (#0072B2) dots in total, stacked in neat columns: 1 dot above 3, 2 dots above 4, 3 dots above 5, 1 dot above 8; no dots above 2, 6, 7 or 9.
The lowest dot (3) and the highest dot (8) have a reddish purple (#CC79A7) ring around them.
Below the line a green (#009E73) bracket runs from 3 to 8, labelled Range = 8 − 3 = 5.
rejection: a number of dots other than 7
dots side by side instead of stacked on repeated values
the range bracket not running from 3 to 8
images.takeaway: Each value is one dot, repeated values stack up, and the range is the gap between the end dots.
images.description: A dot plot on a line from 2 to 9 with 7 dots: one at 3, two at 4, three at 5 and one at 8, and a range bracket from 3 to 8.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Before using the builder, check the equal spacing and count the dots against the data values.

image_decisions.why: A compact picture of the finished dot plot reminds students of the steps before they build their own.
